articles.title: Introducing the Stripe AI Index
articles.summary: Founders have been guessing how much real revenue sits behind the AI boom. Stripe launched a weekly AI Index tracking payments to about 20,000 AI businesses on its platform. Aggregate AI revenue rose 103% over the past year and easily beat the SaaS Index. Median AI growth trailed aggregate growth by a wide margin, so larger AI companies appear to be doing better than typical ones. The index only counts payments through Stripe and tracks weekly shifts as overall growth cools.

articles.title: The new App Store nobody's optimizing for
articles.summary: Apps can now integrate with ChatGPT, allowing interactions without leaving the chat, as seen with partners like Spotify and Expedia. Developers can seize this low-friction distribution channel, ensuring app functions complete quickly and drive users back to their main platform. However, reliance on ChatGPT means limited control over distribution, possible cuts of transactions by OpenAI, and user relationships residing in the chat interface.

articles.title: Your Next GTM Hire Should Be a Creative Marketer.
articles.summary: Cold email volume has exploded now that anyone can launch a massive campaign in minutes with Claude Code. About 91% of cold emails get no replies. A B2B outbound agency reports lifting its reply rate to 15% by targeting signals like a fresh funding round or a new sales leader. Everyone can automate the sending now, so the next hire after a GTM engineer should be a creative marketer who owns the angle and the copy. Teams should score that marketer on replies and message tests.

articles.title: Employee-led content programs are a dangerously good distribution strategy
articles.summary: Employee-led content programs create a ripple effect that can bring any company exponential upside. This post presents a guide on how anyone can get started. What kills these programs are copy-paste captions, forced posting quotas, and posts that only promote the company. People can smell a mandate.

articles.title: How did Lovable grow so fast?
articles.summary: Most founders look for a secret growth playbook behind breakout startups. Lovable turned two this week with over $600 million in annual recurring revenue and no growth hack. The AI app builder rides an exploding category, so tactics that failed at older software companies now work like a raft on a fast river. The lean team ships big updates nearly every week to keep word of mouth moving. New hires are expected to automate the repetitive parts of their own jobs with AI from the start.

articles.title: Building the next generation of automated bidding at Microsoft Advertising (Tool)
articles.summary: Microsoft Advertising is automatically rolling out updated bidding models that adjust nearly twice as fast after target changes. Advertisers on Maximize Conversion Value or Target ROAS see 10% more conversion value per click at similar return, provided they have working conversion tracking with real transaction values.

articles.title: Become a founding member of TLDR's AI community (2 minute form)
articles.summary: TLDR is launching a curated community for AI builders to discuss major news and launches. The best links and comments will be featured in TLDR AI. Apply here to join.

articles.title: Vercel Billing CLI (Tool)
articles.summary: Vercel now groups every billing command under vercel billing in its CLI, covering usage, contracts, and budgets. Teams can check their plan, billing cycle, and balance due, download past invoices, and preview upcoming charges without opening the dashboard. Billing overview and invoice history work on all plans under existing permissions, while upcoming invoice estimates require a paid subscription.

articles.title: The M&A Process | Who, What, and When
articles.summary: Most founders only see the public announcement of an acquisition and rarely hear how messy the private process gets. Company sales start with only top executives and the board in the loop because leaks distract employees and weaken the seller's hand. Choosing an investment bank is a common leak point since banks that lose the pitch often talk. Many deals die early in the process, so keeping the circle tight avoids spooking customers unnecessarily. Bankers and lawyers also cost more than most founders expect.

articles.title: How I used AI to get 25 million views in 7 weeks
articles.summary: Founders often let their social accounts go quiet once daily work takes over. A dormant Threads account reached 25 million views across platforms after an AI loop began drafting new posts from old hit ideas. Raw views converted into far fewer followers on Threads than on Instagram, so select posts offered a free guide and collected 1,745 email addresses. The system scores core ideas and rests each winning idea for at least a month before reposting it.

articles.title: We asked AI the same 210 questions two days in a row. 84% of the answers changed
articles.summary: 84% of AI product answers named different brands the next day, and the top pick held its spot only 63% of the time.

articles.summary: Words like “unlock” and “elevate” now mark copy as AI-written, so give the model real details like the price before it drafts anything.
